sanskrit_verse: ददतो यद भवेत पुण्यं हेमकुप्याम्बरादिकम् । तत स्यात पालयतो न्यासं तथा च शरणागतम् ॥
transliteration: dadato yad bhavet puṇyaṃ hemakupyāmbarādikam | tat syāt pālayato nyāsaṃ tathā ca śaraṇāgatam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: That merit which arises from giving gold, vessels, garments and similar objects, the same arises for one who protects a deposit and also one who seeks refuge.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from capacity to uphold integrity, not mere possession
Causation aligns with conscious intention to preserve dharma
Capacity-based responsibility extends to safeguarding entrusted resources
Restoration logic requires equivalence in protective and giving acts
Consciousness alignment is achieved through honoring trust
executable_legal_axioms: IF an entity receives a deposit THEN it assumes equivalent dharmic liability as a donor of equal value
IF a being seeks shelter THEN the protector holds the same karmic position as a giver of treasure
IF protection is rendered to entrusted property THEN merit accrues as per sacrificial giving
IF refuge is granted THEN no lesser duty applies than that of ritual donation
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes parity between the act of charitable giving and the duty to protect entrusted persons or properties. The threshold of responsibility is determined by the voluntary assumption of care, placing the guardian at the same level of dharma-accountability as the donor. Authority derives from willingness to bear witness to another's vulnerability, thus invoking the court's role to enforce completion rather than punish failure.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that both giving and protecting arise from sankalpa (intention). Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that just as charity leads to expansion of consciousness, so does protection of trust. Proportional responsibility ensures equivalence without punitive overlay. The non-punitive reality rule affirms that all dharmic roles inherently restore balance when executed with awareness.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Re-establish the original intent behind the deposit or refuge
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Align the protector’s sankalpa with the seeker’s vulnerability
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Reinforce the protector’s ability to fulfill the sacred trust
Integrity Reintegration Sequence: Restore mutual recognition of dharma between parties
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority. This law restores Dharma through equivalence of giving and guarding. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
